$comment: §33 to §40. Mission 1.71 refused to invent numbers as though discovered. This is a POLICY mission, so the project chooses its own conservative limits -- and every one carries value_source PROJECT_POLICY_DEFAULT so nobody later reads it as a finding.

selection_principle.principle: the smallest operationally useful initial profile

bounds.why: small enough that one run is reviewable by a person reading its accounting, and large enough that a population is not trivially one site
a bounded pilot on one operator machine; throughput is explicitly not the objective
one request at a time to any one host is the lowest burden a measurement can impose while still finishing
one request every five seconds; deliberately slower than a browsing human
long enough for a slow but working host
bounded so a slow-drip response cannot hold a worker indefinitely
matches the floor RFC 9309 §2.3.1.2 states for robots retrieval, so one number governs both paths and a reader is not comparing two limits

a retry can observe a different world state, and Mission 1.71 deferred the which-attempt-counts rule to the construct. With no construct, zero avoids creating records whose selection rule nobody has decided
64 KiB of headers is far beyond ordinary and finite
1 MiB read cap. This is the NETWORK bound and it applies even though no body is persisted, because not storing is not the same as not receiving
2 MiB across every hop, so a redirect chain cannot multiply the read cap
six hours; a run that cannot finish inside one operator sitting is not a bounded pilot
one fetch per origin, no cache across runs, and it counts toward the origin budget
one initial request plus MAX_REDIRECTS hops. Robots is counted per ORIGIN rather than per target, so it is not included here
explicitly disabled rather than absent, because MAX_RETRIES is 0 and a backoff with nothing to back off from would be a setting nobody could reach

forbidden_values.$comment: §36. A load-bearing limit may not be absent, and absent has many spellings.

retry_reasoning.why_zero: retries create temporal ambiguity, and Mission 1.71 left the which-attempt-defines-the-observation rule to the construct. Choosing a non-zero value now would create records under a selection rule that does not exist.
retry_reasoning.if_a_later_profile_enables_retries: attempts remain individually recorded, per the run contract

body_and_network_interaction.$comment: §39. The trap this bullet exists to close.
